title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche (c. 1981). Here pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, a free group with loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity satisfying l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1. Grothendieck embeds it in its 'modular' envelope S^+_{0,3}, which is PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. That group is generated by sigma_infinity (order 2) and rho (order 3), and pi_{0,3} sits inside it as Gamma(2)/{±1}, a normal subgroup of index 6 with quotient S_3. In the profinite completion, l'_0 = epsilon_0 = sigma_infinity rho is the parabolic generator, and l_0 = (l'_0)^2 generates the inertia subgroup L_0.

The page summarizes the preceding computation as a theorem. Let 'automorphisme extérieur étoilé' mean an outer automorphism that preserves the inertia conjugacy classes. Such an outer automorphism of hat(pi)_{0,3} that commutes with the outer S_3-action has three equivalent descriptions:
(i) it lifts uniquely to a genuine automorphism commuting with sigma_infinity, and commuting with rho modulo inner automorphisms;
(ii) equivalently, it is the restriction of a unique automorphism u of hat(S)^+_{0,3} = hat(PSL_2(Z)). This u fixes sigma_infinity, fixes the image of rho in S_3, and preserves the conjugacy class of the closed subgroup L'_0 = <sigma_infinity rho> (or of L_0).

Such a u is parametrized by:
- a multiplier p in hat(Z)^*, with gamma = (p-1)/2 in hat(Z) (the previous page checks 2-adic integrality);
- an element g_0 in hat(pi)_{0,3}/L_0.

Set h_0 = sigma_infinity(g_0)^{-1} g_0 = [sigma_infinity, g_0^{-1}] (47). The conditions are:
(a) the relation (48): f_0 · rho(f_0) · rho^2(f_0) = 1, where f_0 = l_0^gamma h_0^{-1}. This relation is invariant under g_0 -> g_0 l_0^lambda.
(b) sigma_infinity and g·rho topologically generate hat(S)^+_{0,3}, where g = sigma_infinity(g_0) l_1^gamma rho(g_0)^{-1} = sigma_infinity(g_0 l_0^gamma) rho(g_0^{-1}) (40).

The automorphism is then u(sigma_infinity) = sigma_infinity, u(rho) = g·rho. The NB explains that (48) is just the defining relation (g rho)^3 = 1, i.e. g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1, rewritten in terms of g_0 and gamma, using the presentation sigma^2 = rho^3 = 1.

Note that sigma_infinity(h_0) = h_0^{-1} holds automatically. This is the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1. Relation (48) is the 3-cycle (hexagon) relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1 with m = (lambda-1)/2.

In modern terms, this is exactly the Drinfeld/Ihara description of hat(GT)-type pairs (lambda, f) satisfying relations (I) and (II). It is obtained here as the group of S_3-equivariant, inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of hat(F)_2, realized as automorphisms of hat(PSL_2(Z)).
errors: Notational clash in the transcription: the multiplier is p (the previous page has p = 2gamma+1), not rho. Grothendieck's handwriting makes them look alike, and the transcription wrote 'rho in hat(Z)^*' and 'gamma = (rho-1)/2'.
'(46) ci-dessous' should refer to the relation above, (46), restated here as (48). This is a minor slip, or 'ci-dessus' misread.
Condition (b) (topological generation) is stated but not shown to be automatic or reformulated. Whether it follows from (a) together with p in hat(Z)^* is left open on this page.
The marginal formula for g is partly illegible and seems to be an exploratory rewriting. It is not an error, but its exact form is uncertain.

ideas.what: Realizing S_3-equivariant inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of hat(F)_2 = hat(pi)_{0,3} as genuine automorphisms of hat(PSL_2(Z)) = hat(Z/2 * Z/3) fixing the order-2 generator, with uniqueness of the lift.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type automorphisms via the modular group / extension of GT action to hat(PSL_2(Z)) (Gamma_{1,1}-type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps for the modular-group viewpoint; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki for outer-automorphism characterizations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller-tower / GT programme without these explicit equations; La Longue Marche (partially circulated)

ideas.what: Parametrization of such automorphisms by a pair (p in hat(Z)^*, g_0 mod L_0). It uses h_0 = [sigma_infinity, g_0^{-1}], which automatically satisfies the 2-cycle relation, together with the 3-cycle relation f rho(f) rho^2(f) = 1 for f = l_0^gamma h_0^{-1}, gamma = (p-1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld–Ihara relations (I) f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and (II) the hexagon relation with m=(lambda-1)/2 defining hat(GT)_0 / the Ihara–Drinfeld pairs (lambda,f)

ideas.what: Check that (p-1)/2 lies in hat(Z) for p in hat(Z)^* (on the previous page).

missed.claim: An explicit derivation, apparently around 1981, of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations with m=(lambda-1)/2 characterizing S_3-equivariant inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of hat(F)_2. It is obtained by lifting to automorphisms of hat(PSL_2(Z)). This predates Drinfeld's 1990 introduction of hat(GT) with the same relations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents priority and a distinct conceptual origin of relation (II): it is the order-3 relation in PSL_2(Z), not a pentagon/hexagon coherence. That origin is relevant to the history of GT and to the modular-group approaches (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). Specialists familiar with the Longue Marche, such as Schneps, may already know it, so it is only partly unknown.

missed.claim: Condition (b), that sigma_infinity and g·rho topologically generate hat(PSL_2(Z)), is imposed without analysis. Whether it is automatic given (a) is not settled here.
missed.quote: b) σ_∞ et gρ engendrent top. Ŝ^+_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It concerns whether the endomorphism monoid equals the automorphism group, an analogue of the invertibility question for (lambda,f) in hat(GT).

deep.surprise_reason: The page states cleanly, around 1981, what is essentially the Drinfeld–Ihara (lambda,f) description with relations (I) and (II), derived via hat(PSL_2(Z)). Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is broadly known through the Esquisse and Schneps' work on the Longue Marche, but the explicit modular-group derivation of the hexagon relation as (g rho)^3 = 1 is a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'multiplicateur ρ ∈ Ẑ*' should read 'multiplicateur p ∈ Ẑ*', and γ = (p−1)/2 (also in the NB: γ = (p−1)/2).
